newsitem.title: GERMANY: E. German border guard officers set for trial.
newsitem.headline: E. German border guard officers set for trial.

text.p: High-ranking former East German border guards who were responsible for mines and automatic guns along the former inner German frontier will go on trial soon in Berlin, justice authorities said on Monday.
Charges have been filed against three former colonels and two lieutenant colonels who are accused of accessory to murder.
They belonged to an engineering unit which was responsible for mines and the machine guns which were triggered automatically when people attempted to flee across the border.

The Constitutional Court, Germany's highest, ruled last week that East German leaders could be held legally responsible for border killings, removing an important line of defence for former Politburo members.
The long-awaited ruling meant the court did not agree with charges by former communist officials that united Germany practised "victors' justice" against them.

After the ruling a Berlin court issued arrest warrants against Egon Krenz, east Germany's last hardline communist leader, and three other former Politburo members to prevent them from leaving the country.

Krenz and his co-defendants have been on trial for the past year, accused of responsibility for the deaths of east Germans killed trying to flee to the West over the Berlin Wall or across the Cold War frontier between the two Germanys.
The first effects of the ruling were apparent on Wednesday, when another former east German border guard was arrested.

The extreme secrecy surrounding East Germany's fortified borders has made it impossible to know how many people were shot dead or killed by landmines as they tried to flee west from the 1950s to the fall of the Wall on November 9, 1989.
Berlin courts have convicted 29 lower-ranking guards of murder but given most of them suspended sentences because they were young recruits following orders.
